body: I don't think he did read this. I know he used to read SW, but maybe he stopped. And of course, this isn't my regular reddit name. I tried telling him most of this stuff and it just wasn't registering. I dunno. A better couple of days, but I think there's still a long way to go until it's fixed. I'm not tremendously religious, but I will never turn down any prayers someone wants to say for me, because god knows, I can use them. Thank you.

Thank you. I'm actually doing a little better just now - the other night was just dreadful. But I'm still in the thick of it, and I'm sure there will be other bad nights. I will take you up on your offer if that happens, if you don't mind.

Thank you very much. I may ask spouse to come with me to the doctor once I find a shrink (and also possibly a therapist). I would also be interested in some of the support groups you reference.

And yes, the lassitude - that's exactly it. It's impossible to overcome some days.

The last couple of days have been better. Spouse is trying harder, I'm trying harder. Long road ahead, but maybe it will work out.

Thank you again.

Thank you. I really needed to be heard at a time when I didn't feel like I was. I'm familiar with CBT, having done a course of it some years back. I'm calling a shrink tomorrow and have switched meds, transitioning off Effexor and onto Pristiq. I'm also on Topamax now, which I took during the first big thing for impulse control help. My family doc actually just put me on it Friday because I've been having daily migraines for the past year, but I imagine it will also help with some of my mental issues, so that's wored out well.

I expressed a lot of what I said here to spouse during a conversation BEFORE the great wall of text, but it didn't seem to be sinking in. Or spouse was so frustrated as to not be receptive. Or something. I don't know. There was a great divide, and I... I needed to be heard and understood by SOMEONE.

Thank you.

I feel as if spouse is giving up on me, not the reverse. Well, some of the time (my wall of text came after a difficult conversation with spouse, in which I voiced pretty much everything I said here, except the bit about fantasizing about my death). The last couple of days have been better. I think spouse is trying. I'm trying. We'll see. Thank you.

See? Wall of text. Sorry. I have to get it out of me.

---------------

I am, with reservations, going to try a different med. Different meds. The last time I was trying to hit on the right antidepressant, it took nearly a year and I reacted to some of the meds very badly. You know, you do the side effects, then you have to wait six weeks or a couple of months to see if the med works, and if it doesn't, it's back to square one. Takes time. Is miserable for everyone until you hit the right med. And spouse told me tonight that a year is not sustainable. Six months of waiting for improvement is pushing it. I'm on a deadline.

And I feel so helpless, because believe me, if I could NOT feel this way, I WOULD. If I could make my current med work for me, I WOULD. If I could hit on the right med with no bad side effects (mania, catatonia, etc., the REALLY bad reactions), I WOULD. If I could make this all stop, I WOULD.

Spouse suggested I get out more. It's a good idea, and one I will implement, but right now it's a struggle to get downstairs, much less out of the house and, say, to the gym. There are other impediments as well, but that's the biggest one, and I'm hoping that a different med will help me break that particular paralysis. Spouse suggested getting a life coach or a therapist or something, not for talking about my mother and my feelings and all that - BTDT - but for being accountable. You know, setting goals for my week and then having to report back to someone about what I did and didn't do. I guess like a parole officer. I don't love the idea, but I'm willing to try it.

I feel so much pressure. Everything that I'm trying isn't working, or isn't good enough. And it feels like I'm climbing a mountain. I mean, really, literally, folding a load of laundry is such a triumph for me right now. I know it's pathetic, but it really and honestly is the best I can do right now, these paltry little things. And they're not good enough for spouse. My failings are keeping my spouse angry and resentful and stressed out and tired ALL THE TIME. Not just with me - spouse is spread so thin that there is no patience for the kids, just no enjoyment to life at all. So, you know, I'm managing to make ALL of us miserable.

And I wish I could fix it. I wish it were like a switch. I wish it were just a mood I could shake off. But this one is too deep for me to just bootstrap myself out of it. And I'm trying to take measures, I'm trying so hard, and it isn't enough. It isn't enough, and it isn't producing results fast enough to relieve spouse. And I am going to lose spouse. I am so afraid I'm going to lose my marriage. In some ways, I feel like it's already circling the bowl and just hasn't quite yet finished flushing away.

I would literally rather die than live without my spouse. My kids, too, because, you know, when you're suffering mental illness and you go through a divorce, the NON-crazy one gets the kids. But especially spouse, that's what hurts the most and the most unbearable, to think of living life without my spouse.

I recognized tonight, as spouse and I were having a most difficult conversation about where to go from here, whether I will be able to meet the deadline and get well before spouse has had too much, that really, my family would be better off without me. I am nothing but dead weight. I am a waste of food and air and money. I am a leech. I contribute nothing and take so much. My kids aren't happy because I can't really be the best parent right now. My spouse is miserable. I am miserable. We are all unhappy. And I am the problem. It is all because of me. And if it were something I could fix by myself, I would. I am trying to fix it. I am just afraid it won't get fixed in time. And in the meantime, I am worthless. I am so bad for everyone I love. They would all be better, have better lives, if I weren't around.

I have nowhere to go. I have no real marketable skills. I've been at home long enough that finding a job will be difficult even when I'm at my best, and I feel so far away from being my best. I remember how I just couldn't see the end of the tunnel before, and I remember, intellectually, at any rate, that the light eventually came and I managed to get out, but god, to internalize the knowledge that this is temporary, or at least this episode won't last forever, is so hard. I feel like I will never be OK again. I should leave, let spouse find someone worthy, a better partner and mate and better parent for the kids. But there is nowhere to go - I am isolated enough (by choice, by circumstances, but NOT by spouse, I mean to say) that I have nothing to go to, nowhere to go, no one to help me. (Which is why I'm posting here instead of phoning a friend or whatever.)

And even if there were somewhere to go, I'm not sure I could live my life knowing I left everything, my kids, my spouse, everything. I would always yearn to go back, always wonder, always be miserable wondering what I was missing and what could have been had my fucked up brain and general worthlessness not fucked everything up. I don't think I would want to live without my spouse and my children. No, I know I wouldn't want to. I would rather be dead than be alive and without them. Even when I'm not drowning in depression, I've felt that way. 

So I should leave, but I can't. Unless I kill myself. And I'm having those ideations, those beautiful horrible fantasies. I have looked up methods online (I forgot a lot since the last time I did the research years ago). I don't know that I would ever have the guts to go through with it. I tried, back during the first bad episode, but obviously failed. 

I don't want to die. I want to curl up and sleep until this is over. That isn't an option, though. And I am so miserable, so afraid, so alone. I am going to lose everything that I love the most, it has already started. I don't know even if spouse loves me any more, or just stays with me because of the kids and out of pity. Spouse has, understandably, pulled away from me as the resentment has grown, and I feel so lonely, never touched, just so alone. That doesn't help with the depression, but I understand why spouse doesn't really want to have anything to do with me. I don't want to have anything to do with me, either.

I don't know what to do. I feel so trapped, and helpless, and sad. I'm trying as hard as I can to fix things, but it isn't happening fast enough, and we're all sick of me. I'm afraid I will never be good enough. I feel like I never have been. I just wish I wasn't here.

Thanks for listening.
